threat_scenario: RollJam: jam + capture the first code, replay it later to open the vehicle
attack_path: Attacker near the vehicle with a transmit/receive SDR; on the owner's lock press, jam the 433 MHz band and capture the code (vehicle receives nothing, stays unlocked); on the second press, jam+capture again and replay the first code (vehicle locks, owner leaves); replay the retained second code later to open the vehicle (accepted within the F-05 look-ahead window, A-05)
feasibility_rationale: Consumer SDR (e.g. HackRF, ~300EUR), published technique (RollJam, 2015); requires presence when the owner locks (window of opportunity); relies on A-05 (tolerant look-ahead window)

threat_scenario: Denial jamming: jam the 433 MHz band during the lock command so the BCM receives nothing and the vehicle stays unlocked while the owner believes it is locked
feasibility_rationale: Common jammer or SDR, from radio range, no physical access

threat_scenario: Pair an attacker key via OBD diagnostic, then open the vehicle with it
Pair an attacker key via direct CAN injection (exterior harness), bypassing the gateway, then open the vehicle with it
Revoke the owner keys via OBD diagnostic
Revoke the owner keys via direct CAN injection
Extract K via key-fob debug interface during temporary possession, return the fob, then use the retained clone later to open the vehicle (valet/rental scenario)

asset: Key secrets stored in the BCM (all paired keys)
threat_scenario: Read all stored secrets via BCM debug interface, then clone a key and open the vehicle

asset: Key secrets stored in the BCM (all paired keys)
threat_scenario: Overwrite a stored key record (Key ID + secret) with the attacker key's values via BCM debug, so the attacker fob is accepted and opens the vehicle
Roll the stored counter back via BCM debug, so a previously captured code becomes valid again and opens the vehicle
Flash a backdoored firmware via the BCM debug interface, bypassing RKE authentication and enabling unauthorized door or trunk release
feasibility_rationale: Assumes A-07: no effective firmware authenticity, integrity or debug-access protection blocks the modified firmware

feasibility_rationale: Assumes A-06: the Key ID is stable across successive transmissions
